To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

a single element of the secondary structure of angiogenin (ANG), a 13-reside surface loop, is responsible for its angiogenic and ribonuclease activities, and the loop can be replaced with a similar element from ribonuclease (RNase), a protein that lacks both activities.
a hybrid protein was produced by substituting 13 residues of the surface loop of angiogenin for the corresponding 15 residues of bovine pancreatic ribonuclase A.

a hybrid protein was produced by substituting a 13-residues segment of a surface loop from angiogenin (ANG), an angiogenesis-promoting hormone, for the analogous 13 residues in bovine pancreatic ribo-nuclease A (RNAse).
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of new molecules that modulated neovascularization, a key process in tumor growth and metastasis.
understanding the molecular basis of angiogenesis, a process of fundamental importance in the development and maintenance of the cardiovascular system and in the pathogenesis of many human diseases.
the development of novel molecules that modulate the formation of blood vessel networks.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the replacement of a single surface loop in the structure of RNase with the corresponding surface loop of ANGs leads to the formation of a protein with a noncognitive biological activity.
the replacement of a surface loop endows RNase with an angiogenic activity.
the RNase/ ANG hybrid protein is angiogenic, and the 13-residue ANG peptide inhibits angiogenesis.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have shown that the surface loop of angiogenin, a small protein, is essential for its function and that the surface loop can be replaced with a surface loop of a nonhomologous protein and the hybrid protein will still retain the activity of angiogenin.
a 13-residues loop endows a protein (RNase) with a new biological activity (angiogenesis).
the angiogenic activity of ANG can be replaced by RNase simply by substituting 13 surface loop residues of ANG for the analogous residues of RNase.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a single element of structure is sufficient to endow RNase with angiogenic activity.
a protein can be endowed with a new biological activity simply by changing a single structural element.
a protein can be endowed with a novel biological activity by replacing a small surface loop.
